description: A techno percussion synthesiser with two engines, eight models and eight sounds within each model, playing up to eight overlapping hits from one output

params.text: Chooses one of eight models, which sets the basic material of the hit; the display names the choice
Chooses the engine: physical modelling at the bottom, FM at the top. Switching it silences every hit that has not finished
Chooses one of eight variations within the model; the display names the choice
Sets how long the hit rings, opening out much further over the top half of its travel
Tunes the hit over -2 to +2 octaves; it is read at the moment of the trigger, so turning it does not bend a hit already ringing
Balances the resonant body of the hit against its transient, and sets how quickly the body is damped
Moves the pitch, phase and modulation of the hit while it rings
Sets how much noise goes into the hit
Spreads the pitch of each hit at random around the tuned pitch; at zero every hit lands on the same pitch

inputs.text: A rising edge above 2V fires a hit; the voltage has to fall below 0.1V before another can fire
While patched it replaces the MODEL knob altogether: 0-10V picks one of the eight models in order
While patched it replaces the SOUND knob altogether: 0-10V picks one of the eight sounds in order
Offsets MOTION, 10V covering the knob's full travel
Volt-per-octave pitch added to the TUNE knob, read at the moment of the trigger
Offsets DECAY, 10V covering the knob's full travel
Offsets NOISE, 10V covering the knob's full travel

outputs.text: Every hit that has not finished, summed and held to ±10V

notes: nothing comes out until a hit is fired. Send a trigger to TRIGGER
eight hits can ring at once; a ninth trigger takes over whichever voice has the least left in it
BODY and TUNE VAR are the two shaping knobs with no CV input of their own

inputs.0:
high above 2V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
0 to 10V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.3:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
inputs.4: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
